item.text:
**4B.10 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

**Verdict:** weaker overall, or at best not meaningfully stronger. Srettha’s removal and the orderly handoff to Paetongtarn were constitutional, but the broader democracy picture in 2024 did not improve: the reformist opposition was still blocked/dismantled, rights enforcement stayed weak, media freedom remained constrained, and the coalition depended on military-aligned parties. The main positive is procedural continuity, not a broader strengthening of democratic resilience.

- **Thailand: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/thailand/freedom-world/2024**
  - Claim: Thailand improved from “Not Free” to “Partly Free” because of the competitive 2023 election and formation of a new governing coalition, but unelected senators still blocked the most-voted party from power and civil liberties remained constrained.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.8, 4B.3, 4B.5

- **Thailand | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | June 17, 2024 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand**
  - Claim: Thai media could still criticize government policy and report corruption, which is a real positive sign for democratic resilience.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.3

- **Thailand | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | June 17, 2024 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand**
  - Claim: The same report says media freedom stayed constrained by elites, self-censorship persisted around the military and judiciary, and Pheu Thai’s coalition with military-backed parties eroded trust and democratic optimism.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.3, 4B.5

- **Thailand: New Government Slow to Protect Rights | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights**
  - Claim: HRW said the Srettha government had not made serious rights reforms, while conservative institutions had already blocked Move Forward from forming a government. That indicates weak democratic repair at the start of 2024.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.1, 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.5

- **Thailand’s 2024 report page | Human Rights Watch | 2024 report page | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/thailand**
  - Claim: HRW says the Pheu Thai-led government pledged rights protection but continued past patterns of repression and prosecutions, so the year did not produce a clear democratic deepening.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.5, 4B.6

- **Thai king endorses Paetongtarn Shinawatra as prime minister | Reuters via Investing.com | August 18, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/thai-king-endorses-paetongtarn-shinawatra-as-prime-minister-3576565**
  - Claim: After Srettha’s removal, parliament elected Paetongtarn and the king formally endorsed her two days later. That shows constitutional succession and a non-coup transfer of executive authority.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.8, 4B.1

- **Thai politics braces for shakeup after court dismisses PM Srettha Thavisin | Reuters via Investing.com | August 13-14, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/judgment-day-for-thai-pm-srettha-as-court-rules-on-dismissal-case-3570233**
  - Claim: Reuters said the Constitutional Court dismissed Srettha for an ethics violation tied to a cabinet appointment, and that the ruling threatened a coalition shakeup. This is negative for democratic stability because it shows fragility and elite capture risks, even though the transfer remained constitutional.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.8, 4B.5

- **Victory for Same-Sex Marriage in Thailand | Human Rights Watch | June 18, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/victory-same-sex-marriage-thailand**
  - Claim: Thailand’s Senate approved same-sex marriage under Srettha’s government, which is a concrete legislative rights gain and one of the clearest positive institutional outcomes of 2024.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.7

- **Thailand: Last-Ditch Effort for Tak Bai Massacre Justice | Human Rights Watch | May 1, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice**
  - Claim: Continued impunity for the Tak Bai case showed that minority protection and accountability for state abuses remained weak, which undercuts any claim that democratic resilience had broadly strengthened.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.7, 4B.4, 4B.5

- **Thailand: Investigate Detained Youth Activist’s Death | Human Rights Watch | May 23, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/23/thailand-investigate-detained-youth-activists-death**
  - Claim: Hundreds of monarchy critics remained in pretrial detention, which is evidence that dissent was still being suppressed rather than normalized into a healthier democratic order.
  - QIDs: 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6, 4B.7

**Search gap:** I did not find a Srettha-specific democracy-resilience index for 2024. The conclusion is therefore qualitative, based on a mix of procedural-success evidence and substantial evidence of continuing repression and institutional fragility.
